sentences.text: The primary skull specimen, IGV 33, is believed to belong to an adult individual based on bone fusion. This skull is somewhat elongate, measuring approximately 28 centimeters (11 inches) in length and 13 centimeters (5 inches) at its widest point.
The premaxillae at the snout tip held five teeth each, while the maxillae held 16 or 17 teeth with wide spacing.

The genus was described by Xiao-Chun Wu and colleagues in 2001, with the type species designated as Rugosuchus nonganensis. When first described, Rugosuchus was the most complete crocodyliform known from northeastern China and the second such fossil found in that region.

Wu et al. determined Rugosuchus was not an eusuchian due to palatal bone structure, but suggested it was more closely related to eusuchians than genera like Goniopholis because it possessed more than two rows of bony armor. A 2008 phylogenetic analysis by Turner and Buckley placed Rugosuchus in a clade with Eusuchia alongside the "Glen Rose Form," suggesting it is more derived than Bernissartia. The parent group of Rugosuchus is classified as Paralligatoridae, and the animal belongs to the family Paralligatoridae.

At the time of its description, the age of the formation where Rugosuchus was found was thought to be the latest Early Cretaceous based on associated ostracode, bivalve, and fish fossils. Subsequent studies have generally reclassified the age of the Rugosuchus formation as the Late Cretaceous.
The time range for Rugosuchus is the Campanian stage, spanning from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
